newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to back guards against gene-test bias-Post.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to back guards against gene-test bias-Post.

text.p: President Clinton will endorse a bill that would make it illegal for health insurers to discriminate against healthy people on the basis of their genetic inheritance, the Washington Post reported Monday.

The bill includes more protections against genetic discrimination than those included in a health law passed last year and comes as biological discoveries are giving doctors and researchers increasing ability to predict who may succumb to various inherited diseases.

Clinton's decision to push for heightened protections reflects recommendations in a report to be presented to the president Monday by Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala, the Post quoted White House sources as saying.
The report warns that the potential benefits of genetic testing may never be realised if people reject the tests out of fear that the information may be used against them.

The bill that Clinton will endorse is a slightly modified version of legislation introduced in January by Representative Louise Slaughter, a New York Democrat. Maine Republican Olympia Snowe has introduced an identical bill in the Senate.
